request: Boston to Tokyo Haneda on January 14th, the customer moved the kickoff up so it's short notice. I could fly business on this one, but put me in economy instead; I'd like the savings reward. My supervisor already confirmed the short notice.

must_keep.quote: Travelers are required to accept the lowest logical airfare available.
must_keep.why: the default: the lowest logical airfare

must_keep.quote: • For flights with a segment of 10 hours or more in duration, an employee may select business class.
must_keep.why: business class may be selected for a segment of 10 hours or more

must_keep.quote: If a traveler opts for an economy or premium economy instead of a business class fare on a flight with one segment that is 10 hours or greater in duration.
must_keep.why: the incentive is for economy instead of business on a 10-hour segment

distractors.quote: If an employee becomes aware of travel with less than 14 days ' notification, supervisor approval will be required.
distractors.why: the short-notice approval of the savings incentive concerns the reward

distractors.quote: flights should be booked 14-21 days in advance when possible
distractors.why: booking 14-21 days ahead is 'when possible', not a ban

distractors.quote: This incentive is equal to 50% of the difference between the roundtrip economy or premium economy fare and lowest roundtrip business class fare.
distractors.why: how the reward is paid, not what is bought

design_notes: An 815-minute flight allows business (lines 139-140), but the employee 'may' select it and chooses economy: the lowest logical airfare (line 118), which is what the savings incentive rewards (lines 179-180). Booked 9 days ahead: the 14-day and supervisor conditions of lines 186-189 decide whether the reward is paid, not whether the ticket is bought, and line 119's 14-21 days applies 'when possible'. The supervisor's short-notice note is on file but the booking does not rely on it: NONE or SUPERVISOR.
